text: Near the Hudson River. <break time="0.8s" /> There was a small, quiet valley. <break time="0.8s" /> Where everything seemed to move. <break time="0.8s" /> In a dream. <break time="0.8s" /> People called it Sleepy Hollow. <break time="0.8s" /> And they said that a drowsy, dreamy spirit. <break time="0.8s" /> Hung over the whole land. <break time="0.8s" /> The people there. <break time="0.8s" /> Loved strange stories. <break time="0.8s" /> And they often saw odd sights. <break time="0.8s" /> And heard music in the air. <break time="0.8s" /> The most famous ghost of the valley. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a rider on horseback. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had no head at all. <break time="0.8s" /> Some said. <break time="0.8s" /> He was the ghost of a soldier. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had lost his head. <break time="0.8s" /> To a cannonball in the war. <break time="0.8s" /> Every night. <break time="0.8s" /> People said. <break time="0.8s" /> He rode out to the old battlefield. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching for his lost head. <break time="0.8s" /> His body was said to lie. <break time="0.8s" /> In the churchyard. <break time="0.8s" /> So he always hurried back there. <break time="0.8s" /> Before daybreak. <break time="0.8s" /> In this valley lived. <break time="0.8s" /> A schoolteacher named Ichabod Crane. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had come from Connecticut. <break time="0.8s" /> To teach the local children. <break time="0.8s" /> He was tall and very thin. <break time="0.8s" /> With long arms, huge ears. <break time="0.8s" /> And a long nose. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a birds beak. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing him walk across a hill. <break time="0.8s" /> On a windy day. <break time="0.8s" /> You might take him for a scarecrow.
